who: People reading in a second language
Anyone stressed or in a hurry
takeaways: When text needs reading ability above lower secondary education, roughly nine years of school, there is supplemental content or a simpler version. Proper names and titles are left out when judging the level.
Supplemental content can be a plain-language summary, diagrams, illustrations, or audio or video that explains the same thing.
This is Level AAA. It does not ban complex writing; it asks that a simpler way in is available.
Writers usually own the words. Designers own where the summary or simpler version sits, so people find it before they give up.
failures: Terms and policies written only in legal language
A dense medical explanation with no summary
An “easy read” version hidden at the bottom of a long page
check: Run long text through a readability tool to estimate its level, and confirm with real readers where you can.
For text above the threshold, check a summary or simpler version exists.
Check it is placed where people meet the complex text, such as at the top or as a clear link.

quiz.question: Your privacy policy reads at university level and legal says it must stay as written. How do you meet 3.1.5?
options: Add a plain-language summary at the top, with key points and simple diagrams
Shorten the policy by removing sections
quiz.why: The rule allows the original text to stay if supplemental content or a simpler version is available. Cutting sections may break the legal meaning, and there is no exception for legal text.

spec: Mark which pages need a summary or simpler version, and where it sits on the page.
Design the summary block or the switch between versions.
Note who writes and updates the simpler version when the original changes.
review: Who is this text written for, and who will actually read it?
If someone reads only the first paragraph, do they get the main point?
Who keeps the simple version in step with the full one?
tradeoff: Two versions of a text can drift apart. Start with a short summary of key points, which is cheaper to maintain, and save full simpler versions for high-stakes content like health, money and legal terms.
system: Offer a summary or key-points component for the top of long pages, and a pattern for linking to a simpler version.
pitch: Plain-language summaries help everyone decide faster, and they reduce support requests about what our policies mean.
